claims.text: The degree of short-range ordering governs phase stability in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni high-entropy alloys.
Short-range ordering modulates defect mobility.
Short-range ordering modulates precipitate formation.
Enhanced short-range ordering creates coherent ordered nanodomains within a disordered matrix.
Coherent ordered nanodomains act as energy barriers to defect migration.
The increased migration barriers make irradiation-induced defects more likely to recombine rather than cluster.
Enhanced short-range ordering reduces irradiation-induced defect clustering.
Short-range ordering impedes coarsening or deleterious phase transformations at high temperature.
Impeded coarsening or phase transformation helps retain high-temperature strength.
Ordered domains distribute mechanical stresses more uniformly under cryogenic conditions.
More uniform stress distribution prevents brittle failure and maintains cryogenic toughness.
The as-quenched Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni baseline is a homogeneous, single-phase disordered solid solution with minimal short-range order.
Moderate-temperature annealing around 600°C can enhance short-range ordering without causing full-scale precipitation or phase separation.
The annealed material will contain incipient B2-like short-range-ordered regions and associated local lattice distortions.
Relative to the quenched baseline, the short-range-order-enhanced alloy will develop fewer irradiation-induced dislocation loops.
Relative to the quenched baseline, the short-range-order-enhanced alloy will retain more high-temperature strength.
Relative to the quenched baseline, the short-range-order-enhanced alloy will have greater cryogenic fracture toughness.
The proposed mechanism is limited to conditions that retain a single-phase solid solution while producing moderate short-range order without long-range ordering or unwanted precipitation.
Very high aluminium content may place the alloy outside the regime in which the proposed mechanism applies.
Grain size and residual stress may independently contribute to the measured irradiation and mechanical properties.
